propositions: Pass-1 context-limit escalation silently relocates to bare Anthropic model IDs when the run was configured for a provider-qualified model like Bedrock, bypassing the model-class table lookup

The _rung_target function decides escalation targets by comparing only ladder constants without considering the run's actual configured model, causing provider-qualified primaries to degrade to unqualified bare names
When no model-class table is configured, models_at_or_above returns bare Anthropic family names for Bedrock-qualified inputs, causing provider mismatches in cfg.model assignment during escalation

The entry rung escalation path uses frontier model which resolves to anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, triggering the bare-form substitution on the common one-criterion retry instead of only on rare deep escalation

The fix threads the primary model into _rung_target and applies provider-agreement rule: return primary verbatim if providers differ on the primary's own rung, drop the rung if providers differ on higher rungs
